issues.evidence: The lit area of the disc is a band along the right and lower-right rim, and its inner terminator is concave toward that lit limb — the signature of a crescent. A gibbous phase would show the lit region covering more than half with a convex terminator; that is not what is painted.

uncertainObservations: Pole count is NOT reliable and I am recording it as null. Individually resolvable vertical shafts, left to right: (a) one at the extreme left edge; (b) one left-of-center heavily wrapped with blossoms and a ribbon; (c) a thinner one just behind the figure's hair; (d) an upper segment behind/above her head; (e) the one she leans on, running from her hands to the ground; (f) one immediately to her right; (g) one further right; (h) one near the right margin. That reads as six to eight. Items (d) and (e) may be a single continuous pole broken visually by her hands and hair, and items (a) and (c) are faint enough in the mist that either could be a painted tree trunk rather than a staff. I am not confident enough to commit to a number.
Several poles are cut off by the top edge of the artwork, so their full extent is unknown.
Whether the pale strands around her waist are chain, beads or plant stems cannot be determined.
The number of blossoms at lower left cannot be resolved; they overlap heavily.
